record.original_question: Find a spectral version of Mubayi's theorem for color-critical graphs, and in the special case q = 1 determine the sharp spectral analog when the forbidden color-critical graph F is a specific graph such as a triangle, clique, book, odd cycle, or even wheel.

evidence.quote: Problem 4 (Ning-Zhai [124]). (i) (The general case) Find a spectral version of Mubayi’s result. (ii) (The critical case) For q = 1 ... find the tight spectral versions of Mubayi’s result when F is some particular color-critical subgraph, such as triangle, clique, book, odd cycle or even wheel, etc.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A graph $F$ is called color-critical if there exists an edge $e \in E(F)$ such that $\chi(F-e) < \chi(F)$, where $\chi$ denotes the chromatic number. For an integer $r \ge 2$ and an integer $n \ge r$, let $T_{n,r}$ denote the Turán graph: the complete $r$-partite graph on $n$ vertices whose part sizes differ by at most one. Write $t_r(n) = e(T_{n,r})$.

Mubayi's theorem (supersaturation form). Let $F$ be a color-critical graph with $\chi(F) = r+1 \ge 3$. There exists $n_0 = n_0(F)$ such that for every integer $q$ with $1 \le q \le n/2$ and every $n \ge n_0$, every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with
$$e(G) \ge t_r(n) - q + 1$$
contains at least $q \cdot c(F,n)$ copies of $F$, where $c(F,n)$ denotes the minimum number of copies of $F$ that an edge of $T_{n,r}$ can be added to obtain (the standard Mubayi counting function). Equality is achieved by adding $q-1$ edges inside one part of $T_{n,r}$.

Let $\lambda(G)$ denote the spectral radius (largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix) of a graph $G$.

Problem. 

(i) (General spectral Mubayi.) Establish a spectral analogue of Mubayi's theorem. Specifically, for a color-critical graph $F$ with $\chi(F) = r+1 \ge 3$, determine the smallest function $\phi(F,n,q)$ such that for every integer $q$ with $1 \le q \le n/2$ and every sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with
$$\lambda(G) \ge \lambda(T_{n,r}) - \phi(F,n,q)$$
contains at least $q \cdot c(F,n)$ copies of $F$, and characterize the extremal graphs.

(ii) (Critical case $q=1$.) For each of the following specific color-critical graphs $F$, determine the sharp threshold $\lambda^\ast(F,n)$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\lambda(G) > \lambda^\ast(F,n)$ contains strictly more copies of $F$ than the minimum supersaturation count (equivalently, more than $c(F,n)$ copies), and identify all extremal graphs:
  (a) $F$ is the triangle $K_3$;
  (b) $F$ is a clique $K_{r+1}$ with $r \ge 3$;
  (c) $F$ is a book $B_k$ (the graph consisting of $k$ triangles sharing a common edge);
  (d) $F$ is an odd cycle $C_{2k+1}$ with $k \ge 2$;
  (e) $F$ is an even wheel $W_{2k}$ (the join of a vertex with $C_{2k}$).
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made. The triangle case (q=1) was resolved by Ning–Zhai and extended in subsequent works; further results on books, theta graphs, and disjoint color-critical graphs have appeared. A December 2025 preprint "Spectral supersaturation for color-critical graphs" claims to resolve the general Ning–Zhai problem, providing a spectral counterpart to Mubayi's and Pikhurko–Yilma's supersaturation results, though full peer-reviewed confirmation is pending. Hence the problem is partially solved, with the general case very recently addressed.

status_evidence.snippet: Provides a complete resolution to a problem proposed by Ning–Zhai, establishing a spectral counterpart to Mubayi and Pikhurko–Yilma in the supersaturation setting.
status_evidence.claim: General spectral Mubayi problem recently resolved (preprint).

status_evidence.title: A strengthening of the spectral chromatic critical edge theorem: Books and theta graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp spectral results for books and theta graphs.

status_evidence.title: Spectral Extremal Problem on Disjoint Color-Critical Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral extremal results for disjoint color-critical graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress on color-critical spectral extremal problems.
